about: I recently graduated from Penn State University with a degree in Computer Science. My interests lie in backend systems, embedded software, and full-stack development. During my internship at Amphenol, I developed firmware utilities and a PID control system for high-speed cable testing, working hands-on with I2C devices and low-level C++ code. At Penn State, I led tutoring sessions at the Academic Excellence Center, supporting students in systems programming, data structures, and object-oriented design. I’ve also built projects like a B2B eCommerce platform and a peer-to-peer file-sharing system. I'm passionate about creating efficient, scalable software and excited to bring my skills to impactful engineering roles.

Academic Projects.name: NittanyBusiness E-Commerce Website
Academic Projects.description: A full-stack B2B e-commerce platform built to streamline procurement for SMEs by connecting them with suppliers through an intuitive interface and optimized backend infrastructure.

Academic Projects.name: Peer-to-Peer File Sharing System
Academic Projects.description: A Python-based P2P file-sharing network with chunked transfers, multi-threaded downloads, and built-in integrity checks for fast and reliable file distribution.

Academic Projects.name: Causal Consistency Simulation
Academic Projects.description: A Python-based distributed system that simulates causal consistency across three data centers using Lamport clocks and dependency tracking to enforce the correct order of operations despite network delays.

Academic Projects.name: Dynamic Storage Allocator
Academic Projects.description: A custom C dynamic memory allocator featuring optimized malloc/realloc/free, segregated free lists, and a heap consistency checker for robust memory management.

Academic Projects.name: Linear Device Library
Academic Projects.description: A C-based Linux utility that combines 16 JBODs into a 1 MB linear device with read/write support, LRU caching, and TCP networking for efficient storage access.

Academic Projects.name: Mini CPU
Academic Projects.description: A Verilog-based 5-stage MIPS pipeline with ALU-to-ALU data forwarding and hazard resolution for optimized execution of R-type instructions.

Academic Projects.name: Course Scheduler App
Academic Projects.description: A database-driven course scheduler with role-based access, built using OOP principles, SQL, and a tabbed GUI for organized course and student management.

Personal Projects.name: AI Portfolio Website
Personal Projects.description: A personal website with an integrated AI chatbot that answers questions about my work and experience.

Personal Projects.name: Expense Tracker App
Personal Projects.description: A MERN stack expense tracker web app with real-time transaction updates and seamless backend integration for efficient personal finance management.

Personal Projects.name: Furniture Store App
Personal Projects.description: An iOS AR app for virtual room decor that lets users place, scale, and move life-size furniture models in real-world spaces with saved layouts and guided setup.

Personal Projects.name: Measurement App
Personal Projects.description: An iOS AR measurement app that lets users mark two points in the real world to calculate distances, with logging, undo, and guided setup features.

experience.work:
• Developed a CLI to interface I2C devices, PWM and TC amplifier chips, leveraging their functionality for high speed cable thermal testing
• Engineered robust and scalable wrapper functions in C++ for the chips, facilitating seamless access to all chip features as per datasheet specs
• Devised test setup to simulate real testing environment with PWM logic for empirical data analysis before integration into the thermostream system
• Programmed a customized TC feedback-based PID control algorithm, achieving dynamic temp correction from over ±7°C to ±0.5°C by leveraging PWM chip features to meet strict customer temp thresholds
• Wrote clear documentation, streamlining the transition for other engineers
